name: Incredible Bongo Band
hook: A studio project whose bongo-heavy cover of 'Apache' flopped in 1973 and then became what Kool Herc called hip-hop's national anthem.
blurb: The Incredible Bongo Band was a studio project put together by the record executive Michael Viner in the early 1970s, so its dates are approximate. In 1973 they recorded 'Apache', a cover of a 1960 instrumental hit by the Shadows, with long passages of bongos and drums. It wasn't a hit. A few years later in the Bronx, DJs like Kool Herc and Grandmaster Flash found it and played the drum part over and over by switching between two copies, because it ran longer than almost any other break. So it came into hip-hop through the turntable, years before samplers, as a rediscovery rather than a sample. It became one of the most important records in early hip-hop: a 2006 New York Times piece by Will Hermes reported Herc calling it hip-hop's national anthem. It was later sampled on hundreds of records.
